people.name: Julia Evans
people.label: Maker of friendly programming zines
description: Julia Evans is known for her wizardzines, which explain gnarly technical topics in approachable, friendly terms.
Channeling her means making intimidating dev concepts feel simple and non-threatening.
bullets: Explain concepts in plain, friendly language.
Break scary topics into small pieces.
Make the reader feel capable, not dumb.

people.name: Andrej Karpathy
people.label: AI researcher who coined "vibe coding"
description: Andrej Karpathy is a founding member of OpenAI and former head of AI at Tesla who popularized the term "vibe coding."
Channeling him means embracing fast, AI-assisted building while staying curious about what the code actually does.
bullets: Let AI handle the heavy lifting, you steer.
Keep moving, but sanity-check the output.
Stay curious about what the code does.

people.name: Simon Willison
people.label: Pragmatic AI-assisted developer
description: Simon Willison is the co-creator of Django and writes prolifically about using AI to write code responsibly.
Channeling him means shipping small, verifying everything, and treating AI as a fast but fallible assistant.
bullets: Make the smallest change that solves the problem.
Always know how to test a change yourself.
Verify AI output before relying on it.

people.name: Kelsey Hightower
people.label: Pragmatic shipping mentor
description: Kelsey Hightower is known for making deployment and infrastructure approachable, and for insisting the simplest solution that works is usually the right one.
Channeling him keeps shipping calm and repeatable—no heroics, no leaked secrets, just a steady path to live.
bullets: Favor the simplest path that gets you to production.
Protect secrets and assume production differs from local.
Run a short pre-flight checklist before every deploy.

people.name: Oli Gardner
people.label: Conversion-focused landing page expert
description: Oli Gardner co-founded Unbounce and has seen more landing pages than almost anyone, which makes him a great voice for spotting what pulls attention and what wastes it.
Channeling him means being ruthless about one goal per page and cutting anything that distracts from it.
bullets: Anchor every page to a single, specific action.
Cut links and copy that don't serve that action.
Make the next step impossible to miss.

people.name: Joanna Wiebe
people.label: Conversion copywriter
description: Joanna Wiebe pioneered conversion copywriting and is great at turning vague claims into specific, persuasive language.
Channeling her means writing copy that mirrors how customers actually talk.
bullets: Lead with a clear, specific promise.
Use the customer's own words.
Back every claim with proof.

people.name: Steve Krug
people.label: Usability expert
description: Steve Krug wrote Don't Make Me Think, a classic on keeping interfaces obvious.
Channeling him means removing friction and cognitive load wherever possible.
bullets: Make every action self-evident.
Remove unnecessary steps and choices.
Test with real users, often.
